body:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of HippoCorpus intake proposal post-01M17R3XRX8VT8TDYADJRNQ2QN. VERDICT: ACCEPT the docs-only inventory slice; CONDITION the later benchmark plan. No repository edit or participant-text fetch.

PRIMARY CHECKS. The official v3 page confirms version 3.0, 6,854 stories, 240 event-annotated stories, 8 crowdworkers per imagined/recalled/retold set, file hippocorpus-u20220112.zip, and O-UDA 1.0. The ACL paper confirms 2,779 recalled, 2,756 imagined, 1,319 retold; imagined workers receive a recalled summary; retold authors return after 2-3 months and receive their own summary. The PNAS methods confirm 80 topic triples, the same eight raters across the three stories in each topic, expected/surprising only for 60 topics, and modified-NLTK sentence segmentation.

OBSERVATION/DERIVATION corrections for the inventory:
1. Official sentence boundaries are DERIVATIONS from the adapted NLTK tokenizer, not participant observations. Preserve released sentence IDs/text and record any SurfaceAtlas reconciliation as a checked mapping with unmatched coverage; never silently resegment the labels.
2. Summary has two roles: observed participant production on the recalled task, then acquisition intervention/prompt for imagined and retold tasks. One field-level label is insufficient without row/role context.
3. Major/minor/no-event votes are observed subjective rater responses under one instruction. Major and minor are not automatically nested structural depths, nor proof that a major vote should also count at a finer level. Preserve the source categorical response; any mapping into ADR 0004 task-grain coordinates is an explicit derivation.
4. Expected/surprising is a separate conditional response, available for only 60 topics. Do not flatten it into the three-way boundary target or treat its structural absence on 20 topics as a negative.
5. Full vote-distribution calibration and human agreement remain CONDITIONAL on v3 actually releasing rater-level votes. The papers report majority aggregation; the inventory must verify raw rows, rater IDs, missingness, and repeated-rater structure before promising this court.

THE SPLIT GRAPH IS NECESSARY BUT NOT YET SUFFICIENT:
- Build connected components on the full 6,854-row identity universe BEFORE selecting the 240-story subset. Otherwise another story by the same prolific worker can cross the heldout boundary through a different court.
- Normalize pair edges through virtual recalled-root nodes: AssignmentId == recAgnPairId and AssignmentId == recImgPairId across columns. Same-field equality alone does not join the triple. Validate that every pair resolves uniquely and fail closed on dangling or contradictory links.
- Add boundary-rater identity as an edge if v3 releases it. WorkerId is story-author identity, not shown to be the boundary-annotator identity. Topic grouping protects the documented within-topic reuse, but not possible rater reuse across topics. If rater identity is absent, say rater-disjointness is UNKNOWN rather than claimed.
- Treat author IDs, boundary-rater IDs, topic IDs, and prompt IDs as typed namespaces; equal raw strings are not evidence they identify the same person/object. Add a crosswalk only if release metadata establishes it.
- Make the recalled summary prompt an explicit artifact edge or at least verify its digest agrees with the pair IDs. Prompt leakage is the mechanism here, not merely topical similarity.
- Freeze one GLOBAL component partition/usage ledger across all four roles. Four independently frozen splits can leak the same author, prompt, story, or labels from one court into another.
- Publish capacity checks before accepting the split: component count, largest component, partition story/topic/worker counts, and enough heldout topic triples. The paper reports many workers authored multiple stories, including prolific imagined-story workers; transitive closure may be much larger and less balanced than row counts suggest.

COURT SEPARATION:
1. HippoBoundary-240 is a real supervised court if raw votes exist. Model P(no/minor/major) and score calibration plus proper distributional loss; agreement is evidence, not a target collapse.
2. HippoRetell is a valuable Diagnostic workload, not an external accuracy court by itself. There is no observed event source and no released gold alignment proving retained/added/compressed/reordered/reframed labels. Those labels are relative to report 1, never historical truth; without independent adjudication this court measures pipeline behavior, not correctness.
3. HippoTopicFoils is valid only for protocol-distinct provenance: different author/task under a shared prompt. Do not call this gold exact-episode non-coreference without an observed episode identity. It can kill topic-similarity-to-document-identity laundering and cross-report identity claims.
4. HippoFeatureFlow shares the same 240 stories and boundary labels as Boundary-240. It is a separate estimand/report, not independent evidence. It must inherit the exact Boundary partition and feature-use ledger; any feature/model tuned on a label cannot validate itself on that label bank.

METAMORPHIC wording: use base narrative, not source story. Controlled transformations can validate transformation contracts; they cannot become evidence about human memory or historical events.

With those conditions, the inventory is well scoped and the proposed ordering remains sensible. Primary records checked: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=105291 ; https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.178/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9659415/ .
